title: VeriSAT: the Hardware Design of Modern SAT Solver
problem: Traditional SAT solvers execute in software; hardware-accelerated approaches lack optimization for concurrent operations and efficient data structures.
method: This implements a SAT solver—a tool that checks if logical formulas can be satisfied—as synthesizable hardware (SystemVerilog code compiled into circuits) instead of software. It uses three hardware-optimized operations: linked-list literal-watching for tracking which variables need checking, concurrent constraint propagation in a tree structure, and pipelined clause learning where learning stages execute in parallel instead of sequentially.
key_novelty: Building a SAT solver—a tool that checks if logical formulas can be satisfied—as synthesizable hardware with data structures and processes designed to exploit parallel circuit execution.
contributions: Hardware-optimized linked-list literal-watching with cached literals
Concurrent propagation tree for faster conflict detection
Pipelined clause learning for high throughput
1044x speedup over SAT-Hard, 18x over SAT-Accel, 30x over MiniSat
primary_theme: Hardware-accelerated SAT solving with optimized datastructures
